performers: Chorus and Orchestra of La Scala; Tullio Serafin; Norberto Mola, chorus master
intro: Captive Hebrews in Babylon send their thoughts home to the Jordan and the fallen towers of Zion. Verdi gives the crowd a shared melody, sung here by the Chorus of La Scala under Tullio Serafin.

cues.title: Before the voices
cues.text: An orchestral introduction, marked Largo. Short rising figures and emphatic repeated chords precede the singers’ long melody; the introduction ends with a pause.
cues.evidence: Verdi, Va, pensiero, vocal score reproduced by El Atril and Free-scores, p. 1, bars 1–11: Largo, repeated chords, rising figures and a fermata before the choral entry. https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3f/Va_pensiero%2C_from_Nabucco%2C_by_Verdi.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: One melody, four voices
cues.text: Sopranos, altos, tenors and basses share the same tune in octaves. Solera’s words send their thoughts towards the hills of home, the Jordan and Zion’s ruined towers. The whole captive population sings with one voice.
cues.evidence: Verdi, Va, pensiero, El Atril/Free-scores vocal score, pp. 2–5, bars 12–28, shows the shared melody. The Italian text and translation appear in the Cleveland Orchestra’s work page: https://www.clevelandorchestra.com/works/verdi-va-pensiero-from-nabucco
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: La Scala, March 1842
cues.text: The opera first reaches La Scala on 9 March 1842 as Nabucodonosor. Giuseppina Strepponi, Verdi’s future wife, is among the singers. More than a century later, the same theatre’s chorus and orchestra make this recording with Serafin.
cues.evidence: Raffaele Mellace’s chronology in La Scala’s 2026 Nabucodonosor study guide gives the original title and première date: https://www.teatroallascala.org/static/upload/dis/dispensa-nabuccol.pdf. William Weaver’s Angel 35265 booklet names Strepponi at the première, identifies her as Verdi’s later wife and documents the June 1955 session: https://archive.org/download/lp_la-scala-presents-verdi-operas-the-great-c_coro-del-teatro-alla-scala-orchestra-del-t/lp_la-scala-presents-verdi-operas-the-great-c_coro-del-teatro-alla-scala-orchestra-del-t_djvu.txt

cues.title: Strength to endure
cues.text: The final stanza asks for a song that brings strength in suffering. Verdi repeats its last words, al patire virtù, and lets the chorus grow softer, until the voices settle into quiet harmony.
cues.evidence: Solera’s final stanza is printed in the Cleveland Orchestra’s work page: https://www.clevelandorchestra.com/works/verdi-va-pensiero-from-nabucco. The El Atril/Free-scores vocal score, pp. 9–11, from bar 41 to the end, shows the repeated text, decrescendo and final choral chords: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3f/Va_pensiero%2C_from_Nabucco%2C_by_Verdi.pdf
cues.how: About the passage as a whole.

fields.label: Performers
fields.value: Chorus of La Scala (chorus), Orchestra of La Scala (orchestra), Tullio Serafin (conductor), Norberto Mola (chorus master)
fields.note: The original cover and booklet credit the Chorus and Orchestra of La Scala, Tullio Serafin and chorus master Norberto Mola. Internet Archive uses the equivalent Italian ensemble names Coro Del Teatro Alla Scala and Orchestra Del Teatro Alla Scala. No individual choristers or orchestral players are identified.

fields.label: Work version
fields.value: Italian-language chorus with orchestra, presented as a separate LP selection
fields.note: The selection includes the chorus’s orchestral introduction and closing cadence. Zaccaria’s ensuing prophecy, joined to the chorus in the opera’s dramatic design, is outside this selection. The performing edition and any small editorial alterations are unidentified. Section joins are broad score-proportional estimates informed by the required audio analysis; they have no bar-level alignment or aural review.

fields.label: Recorded
fields.note: The original booklet states ‘Recorded June 1955 at La Scala with full orchestra and chorus.’ Youngrok Lee’s discography gives 6–7 June for these choruses, but the primary source supports month precision; a particular day and take for this track remain unidentified. The 2021 digitisation is separate.

fields.label: Place
fields.note: The booklet explicitly names La Scala as the recording venue. A particular room, stage configuration or microphone layout is not established.

fields.label: Label
fields.note: The source is an Angel mono vinyl LP, La Scala Presents Verdi Operas: The Great Choruses.

fields.label: Catalogue
fields.note: Internet Archive dates the US issue 1955; Recordsale dates Angel 35265 to 1956. The original booklet’s ©1955 notice concerns its publication material and is kept distinct from proof of an exact release date. The later catalogue year, 1956, supplies the conservative publication year for the recording-rights assessment.

fields.label: Matrix, take, sides
fields.note: The booklet places Nabucco first on side one, matching the selected 01.01 MP3 derivative. Pressing matrix, stamper, original tape identifier and session take are unknown.

fields.label: Transfer
fields.note: The item credits Internet Archive and identifies its LP digitisation workflow. Operator account identifiers are not expanded into unverified personal mastering credits.

fields.label: Transfer date
fields.note: The ripping_date field is 20210617045418. The item’s 31 May 2021 scan/publication date and the derivative’s 2023 processing timestamp are separate events, not recording-session dates.

fields.label: Composition rights
fields.value: Verdi’s composition and Solera’s Italian text are in the public domain under ordinary life-plus-70 terms.
fields.note: The opera was composed in 1841 and first published in 1842. Solera died in 1878 and Verdi in 1901. This assessment concerns their original music and text; unidentified modern editions and translations have separate rights.

fields.label: Recording rights
fields.value: Territorial EU public-domain basis: commercial publication in 1955–56, before 1963.
fields.note: The transferred commercial Angel 35265 issue is dated 1955 by Internet Archive and 1956 by Recordsale. Both dates precede 1963; source.rights uses 1956 conservatively. Under the project’s EU rule the former 50-year phonogram term expired before the extension applicable to recordings still protected on 1 November 2013. The booklet identifies the performers and June 1955 session independently of the release dating. Internet Archive supplies no Creative Commons licence. US recording status and worldwide clearance are not established.

composer.born: 10 October 1813, Le Roncole, near Busseto (then in the French Empire)
composer.epithet: He could make a catchy tenor tune sound like a death sentence simply by letting the wrong man hear it.
facts: Provesi in Busseto; private lessons with Lavigna after Milan’s Conservatoire rejected him
Milan · Venice · Florence · Rome · Naples · Paris · St Petersburg · Cairo
Piave, Cammarano and Boito were his principal collaborators
Operas from Oberto (1839) to Falstaff (1893); the Requiem, sacred music, songs and a string quartet
composer.background:
Milan’s Conservatoire turned Giuseppe Verdi down in 1832. Antonio Barezzi, a merchant from Busseto who had helped pay for his move to Milan, kept supporting him, and Verdi studied privately with Vincenzo Lavigna, formerly a musician at La Scala. He learnt counterpoint and went to the theatre. Four years later he married Barezzi’s daughter Margherita and took a municipal musical post in Busseto. His patrons were people who had heard him play, watched him grow up and put their own money behind him.

His parents kept an inn and shop at Le Roncole, where he was born in 1813. He learnt the organ locally, then studied with Ferdinando Provesi in nearby Busseto. Oberto, his first opera, reached La Scala in 1839 and earned him further commissions. His daughter Virginia had died in 1838; his son Icilio died in 1839, and Margherita in June 1840. That September the theatre presented his comedy Un giorno di regno. It failed. Verdi was twenty-six and had lost his wife and both children.
